relevance.rationale: SLq(2) knot model of elementary particles: the closest published analogue to QOU's own knot-as-particle construction, and an explicitly owner-requested read (docs/audits/2026-08-03-eightfold-way-a2-q-deformation-dialog-assessment.md line 532 lists it under 'Want'). It supplies a CANDIDATE, not a result QOU consumes: an explicit second diagram invariant (the rotation/Whitney number r) alongside the writhe w, with a published charge assignment Q_e = -(e/6)(w + r + 1). That is exactly the shape of the missing datum named in conj:sm-hypercharge-invariant ('Y does not factor through the writhe'; the currently-recorded candidate is the ribbon-framing twist, cite bilson-thompson2005). Held to 'supporting' rather than 'core' because Finkelstein's correspondence is FITTED, not derived: he states (p.5) that the trefoil-to-family ordering is chosen so that a single k = e/3 works ('If one aligns the trefoils and the families in any other relative order, one needs more than one value of k'). Per the block's own rule, a candidate that requires tuning a coupling is a fit and does not instantiate the class. QOU may adopt the INVARIANT (r) as a candidate to run through the two batteries; it must not adopt the numerology. No ref() entry exists; the corpus's only preon entries are the two duplicate Bilson-Thompson keys (bilson-thompson2005 line 5363, bilson-thompson2005 line 7784).

keyResults.statement: The SLq(2) irrep labels are identified with knot-diagram invariants by j = N/2, m = w/2, m' = (r+1)/2, where N = crossing number, w = writhe, r = rotation (Whitney degree).
keyResults.useForFolio: Supplies the rotation number r as a published second crossing-diagram invariant, independent of the writhe — a concrete alternative to the ribbon-framing twist currently recorded (without endorsement) as the candidate second datum in conj:sm-hypercharge-invariant. Feeds bean qou-q377 (twist-vs-writhe as candidate second crossing invariant).

keyResults.statement: t = N/6, t_3 = -w/6, t_0 = -(r+1)/6, Q_e = -(e/6)(w + r + 1), consistent with the Standard-Model relation Q_e = e(t_3 + t_0).
keyResults.useForFolio: A published writhe+rotation -> (I_3, Y, Q) assignment that can be run directly through the two batteries conj:sm-hypercharge-invariant demands — Gell-Mann-Nishijima consistency on the nucleon doublet, and the first-generation hypercharge spectrum with its Z_6 relations. Its failure or success on the p/n doublet (which share Y = +1 but differ in writhe) is a cheap, decisive test.

proposedActions.rationale: Orphan: no ref() entry despite being an explicitly named 'Want' in the eightfold-way dialog assessment and the closest published analogue to the QOU construction. Suggested id finkelstein2008 (Int. J. Mod. Phys. A 24 (2009) 2307).

The block records the ribbon-framing twist as the sole candidate second datum, citing bilson-thompson2005 as literature precedent. Finkelstein's rotation number r is a second, independent published candidate for the same slot and belongs in the same sentence — recorded without endorsement, with the fitted-ordering caveat stated.

Evaluate Q_e = -(e/6)(w + r + 1) and t_0 = -(r+1)/6 on the QOU proton/neutron knot states: the nucleon doublet is the recorded falsification for writhe-only Y, so whether adding r separates it is a one-shot decisive test of the candidate. A pass does not wire it (the correspondence is fitted upstream); a fail prunes the candidate.
